title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to choose safe and healthy foods to ensure the well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we'll provide information on foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly to avoid health risks.

## Foods to Limit
According to reputable sources like the CDC, NHS, and FDA, there are certain foods that pregnant women should limit or avoid eating during pregnancy. Here are some examples:

* Deli meats and hot dogs: These foods can contain Listeria bacteria, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.
* Unpasteurized dairy products: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain bacteria like E. coli and Salmonella, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.
* High-mercury fish: High-mercury fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can contain high levels of mercury, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.
* Undercooked foods: Undercooked foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs can contain bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli, which can cause health problems for mother and baby.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
To ensure food safety, pregnant women should cook the following foods thoroughly:

* Meat and poultry: Cook meat and poultry to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure that bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli are killed.
* Eggs: Cook eggs to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure that bacteria like Salmonella are killed.
* Seafood: Cook seafood to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to ensure that bacteria like Vibrio are killed.

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help pregnant women choose safe and healthy foods:

* Read food labels: Read food labels to ensure that the food has been pasteurized and does not contain harmful bacteria.
* Choose fresh foods: Choose fresh foods and avoid processed or canned foods.
* Cook foods thoroughly: Cook foods to the recommended internal temperature to ensure that bacteria are killed.
* Consult a healthcare provider: Consult a healthcare provider or registered dietitian for personalized nutrition advice during pregnancy.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about their diet during pregnancy, they should seek help from a healthcare provider or registered dietitian. They can provide personalized advice and guidance on choosing safe and healthy foods.

## Reliable Sources
For more information on food safety during pregnancy, pregnant women can consult reputable sources like the [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/), [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/), and [FDA](https://www.fda.gov/).
